**Finding submitted: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

- **What the document does:** Section 13 (p0088) vests all IP in the Work in Garman, expressly including "any Improvements or **Modifications**" — the Modifications are those set out in Schedule "D" (definition p0014), i.e. work we specify and pay for. Our only offsetting rights are the Section 2 non-exclusive, non-transferable object-code use licence tied to Authorized Locations (p0028) and the Section 16(b) source-code licence (p0115), which is only usable on Garman's default, cessation of support or bankruptcy.
- **Gap vs. playbook:** No perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free right to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables we fund (fallback fails), and no statement that we retain rights in our data even though Section 4(b) has Garman converting Sparkling's data. Confidentiality (Section 14) is mutual and does not vest our information in Garman, and there is no assignment of our IP/data or joint ownership — so this is a deviation, not walk-away.
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** a new paragraph after Section 13 granting a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Modifications and other materials developed for us, confirming we retain all rights in our data (including converted data), and excluding joint ownership. Fallback level chosen because the Modifications are changes to Garman's own platform, making an assignment disproportionate.
